parts: I committed to the wrong branch. How do I undo the last commit but keep my changes?

thoughts.content: They want to keep the changes, so `--soft` (staged) or the default `--mixed` (unstaged). Mention moving the commit to another branch, and warn about pushed commits.

parts:
Use a soft reset. It moves the branch back one commit and leaves your changes staged:

```sh
git reset --soft HEAD~1
```

Then switch to the right branch and commit again:

```sh
git switch feature/login
git commit -m "Add login form"
```

| Command | Changes end up |
|---|---|
| `git reset --soft HEAD~1` | staged |
| `git reset HEAD~1` | unstaged (working tree) |
| `git reset --hard HEAD~1` | **deleted** |

If you already pushed the commit, prefer `git revert HEAD`, which doesn't rewrite shared history.
And if I want to undo the reset itself?

The old commit is still in the reflog. Find it and reset back to it:

```sh
git reflog
git reset --soft HEAD@{1}
```
